items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1959-03-18
items.q: Well, the next time, I came from Paul Barberin and do nothing much, so I just accepted it. And I've been with them ever since.

ctx.x: I worked around, well, I worked, yeah, I worked around, on Decatur Street, they had a lot of joints on Decatur Street, before Budapest Street got popped in. I played around there with a lot of three and four-piece bands. I played around there with Johnny St. Sarah too. Johnny St. Sarah played with me an old Lego band one time.
When did you join Bill Matthews? How long has that been now?
Well, a rough guess, I think it's about five years.

items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1962-01-04
items.q: It wasn't Bill Matthews on the job

ctx.x: And you put in some variations on the ground. Oh yeah. You can jazz it up, you know.

It's got two little melodies in there. What about Decatur Street? I think you mentioned something about that one still playing over there. Oh yeah. Decatur Street one time was just like Boydham Street. It wasn't Boydham Street, it was Decatur Street. Everything was on Decatur Street. They had joints with three, four piece bands. And then, that was every night. Did you ever work at Popeyes or Kingsbury? Yeah. Around those places? Oh, I worked in other places around there. I don't remember working at Popeyes or…
